title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nvidia shares tumbled as much as 14% intraday Thursday before closing down 5.4% after CEO Jensen Huang resigned; the Nasdaq slid 0.4%, S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and the Dow lost 0.3% as the scandal rattled AI-linked names.

Markets: Gold cratered to a 52-week low ($3,889.40/oz, -$113.60) on its third straight down session, pressured by rising Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, and traders cashing out winners to cover tech losses; the 10-year yield climbed further amid fading odds of a US-Iran deal.

Companies: Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and director Harvey Jones board chair after Huang's abrupt exit from both the C-suite and the board; rivals AMD and Broadcom gained on the news while Micron and CoreWeave, both tied to Nvidia's ecosystem, fell. Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday.

Companies: Anthropic is still pushing ahead with its Nasdaq IPO (ticker ANT), reportedly targeting a listing before Thanksgiving at a $1.5-2T valuation, despite the AI-stock selloff - seen as a key test of Wall Street's continued faith in the AI trade.

Macro/Policy: Axios scoop - Commerce Secretary Lutnick has repeatedly stalled a Trump-ordered crackdown on firms (including Megaspeed) accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China, despite pushback from Bessent, Hegseth, and Rubio; Senate Democrats are demanding records as the chip-diversion/espionage scandal around Huang widens.

Macro/Policy: Trump said the US doesn't need an Iran deal and directed VP Vance to probe Democrat-run cities/states instead, adding to inflation and oil-supply uncertainty (crude ~$89/bbl, +2.8%) and keeping Fed December rate-cut odds muddled.
